io_driver_functions.notes: Primitive SRAM reader, called as (media_addr, ram_dest_ptr, size, bank) at every observed call site; copies 0x0E000000-relative bytes into a RAM destination. No Flash command bytes (0x5555/0x2AAA) or DMA3 (0x040000D4) programming anywhere in ghidra/decompiled.c, which rules out Flash/EEPROM for this title and supports plain SRAM classification.
Write-and-verify wrapper: calls FUN_080d81b8 to copy RAM->SRAM then reads back via func_0x080da7c0 to confirm, retrying up to 3 times before giving up. Called as (ram_src, media_dest, size[, bank]).
Raw byte-copy primitive underneath FUN_080d82dc; body not resolved in this excerpt (no disassembly shown beyond the call-site argument shape), inferred role is the actual memcpy-to-SRAM step.

Not a checksum in the arithmetic sense - this is the 16-byte magic-signature compare/verify routine, used as a precondition gate before both traced field readers. Classified under 'checksum' role per schema enum since 'verify' is not an available role value; it performs integrity gating, not an arithmetic checksum.

Bulk restore: copies the whole save region from 0x0E000000 into a RAM buffer in 0x1000-byte chunks via FUN_080d82dc, then overwrites the final 16 bytes of the RAM buffer with a ROM constant and re-writes that 16-byte magic back to SRAM offset 0. No traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json; likely invoked from untraced higher-level boot/corrupt-save-recovery code.
Sets bit 6 of a 1-byte SRAM status flag (read-modify-write via func_0x080da7c0 + func_0x080d82dc). Used as the 'write in progress' guard set before the FUN_080138fc field commit.
Clears bit 6 of the same 1-byte SRAM status flag. Used as the 'commit complete' guard cleared after the FUN_080138fc field commit.
Tests bit 6 of the 1-byte SRAM status flag, returns ~(byte>>bit)&1. Used as a read-gate precondition in both traced field-reader functions.
Reads a 4-byte field at RAM-struct offset +0x60 from SRAM, gated by (magic valid AND status bit 6 true). No traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json.
Reads a 4-byte field at RAM-struct offset +0x4d0 from SRAM, gated by (magic valid AND status bit 6 true). No traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json.
Transactional writer for the same +0x4d0 field read by 0x08013930: sets status bit 6, commits 4 bytes RAM->SRAM via FUN_080d82dc, then clears status bit 6. No traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json.

fields.name: magic_signature
fields.update_mechanism: Re-stamped unconditionally by FUN_08001004 at the end of a bulk-restore pass; verified on every gated-read path (FUN_080137cc, FUN_08013930) via FUN_08001094's 16-byte compare against a ROM constant pointed to by _DAT_080010c4 (literal value of that constant is not printed in ghidra/decompiled.c, so the content match is proven by direct byte observation in both .sav files, not by reading the ROM constant itself).
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:404-431 (FUN_08001094 compare routine) and ghidra/decompiled.c:359-397 (FUN_08001004 writer); byte-identical 16-byte ASCII run at offset 0 in both saves/cap-00-future-0.sav and saves/cap-01-future-1.sav per saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt

open_questions: What are the literal values of the opaque DAT constants (_DAT_08013804, _DAT_08013808, _DAT_0801392c, _DAT_08013970, _DAT_0801396c, _DAT_08001120, _DAT_08001160, _DAT_08001190, _DAT_080010c4) that would resolve the gated_field_plus_0x60, gated_field_plus_0x4d0, and status_flag_bit6 fields to absolute SRAM file offsets? Requires a live memory/ROM-data dump beyond what ghidra/decompiled.c exposes.

Does any checksum/CRC exist over a region that happens to be all-zero in both current .sav samples, making it invisible to the byte-diff-based search in Section 4.2? Requires additional, more varied .sav captures with non-zero bytes outside offsets 0x0000-0x000F and 0x1AFC.

What is the semantic meaning of the single mutating byte at offset 0x1AFC (flag vs. monotonic counter vs. enum/index)? Requires paired .ss save states (currently absent for this cohort) and a longer multi-sample capture series.

Do _DAT_08013800, _DAT_08013928, and _DAT_08013968 (the three RAM struct base pointers used by FUN_080137cc/FUN_080138fc/FUN_08013930) alias the same in-RAM save struct, or are they three independent structures? Requires EWRAM/IWRAM memory-map evidence not present in this workspace.

Are FUN_080137cc, FUN_08013930, and FUN_08001004 actually reachable from gameplay in this title, given none of them have a traced caller in ghidra/callgraph.json? Requires either a larger decompilation window or runtime call-trace evidence beyond the 115-function excerpt provided.
